types.name: IUniTextResolver
types.summary: Hook that can override the source text of a [[UniTextBase]] before it is parsed, shaped and laid out — without touching the serialized text field.
types.remarks: Typical use cases: editor-time localization preview (swap keys for translated strings without dirtying scenes or prefabs), runtime localization bound to a language signal, or any derived-text scenario where the authored text is a template or key. Assign via [[TextResolver]]. When a resolver is attached and [[TryResolve]] returns, the component renders the override; the serialized text remains untouched, so scenes and prefabs are not marked dirty. Threading — same two-phase contract as [[BaseModifier]]: [[PrepareForParallel]] always runs on the main thread. Override to cache values from Unity APIs that are main-thread-only (localization tables, ScriptableObject lookups, AssetDatabase in editor). [[TryResolve]] may run on a worker thread when batched parallel processing is active. Do not call Unity APIs directly from it — read from caches populated in [[PrepareForParallel]]. To trigger a rebuild when your external source changes (language switch, scriptable object edit, etc.) call owner.SetDirty(UniTextDirtyFlags.Text) — the owner is supplied to [[OnAttached]].

methods.name: OnAttached
methods.summary: Called after the resolver has been assigned to owner. Use this to cache the owner reference and subscribe to any external signal that should trigger a re-resolve (e.g. a localization language-changed event).

params.name: owner
params.description: The component this resolver is now attached to.

methods.name: OnDetached
methods.summary: Called when the resolver is replaced, cleared, or its owner is destroyed. Unsubscribe from any signals registered in [[OnAttached]].

params.name: owner
params.description: The component this resolver is being detached from.

methods.name: PrepareForParallel
methods.summary: Called on the main thread before parallel processing begins, once per rebuild. Override to cache values from Unity APIs that are main-thread-only so that [[TryResolve]] can read them without touching the Unity API.

methods.name: TryResolve
methods.summary: Produces the effective text to feed into the parsing pipeline.
methods.remarks: May be invoked on a worker thread when batched parallel processing is active. Do not call Unity APIs directly — populate caches in [[PrepareForParallel]] and read them here.
methods.returns: to use result as the text to render; to pass source through unchanged.

params.name: source
params.description: The current source text of the owner (the serialized text field or the buffer set via [[SetText]]).

params.name: result
params.description: When the method returns, receives the override text. The memory must remain valid until the next [[TryResolve]] call on this component or until [[OnDetached]] is invoked.

types.name: LanguageRegistry

types.remarks: HarfBuzz language handles (hb_language_t) are opaque pointers cached internally by HarfBuzz, so equal BCP 47 strings resolve to the same pointer. HarfBuzz maps BCP 47 to OpenType language tags (e.g. zh-Hans → ZHS, ja → JAN) automatically, which drives the locl GSUB feature in pan-CJK fonts. The registry is additive: once a tag is registered, its index stays stable for the lifetime of the process. Index 0 is reserved for "unset" and maps to HB_LANGUAGE_INVALID.

types.summary: Processes Unicode text through script analysis, BiDi reordering, shaping, and layout.
types.remarks: [[TextProcessor]] is the main entry point for the text processing pipeline. It orchestrates multiple Unicode algorithms to produce correctly shaped and positioned glyphs. Processing pipeline: Parsing — converts UTF-16 to codepoints Script analysis (UAX #24) — identifies script per codepoint BiDi algorithm (UAX #9) — determines text direction and reordering Itemization — splits text into runs by script, direction, and font Shaping — converts codepoints to positioned glyphs via HarfBuzz Line breaking (UAX #14) — determines line break opportunities Layout — positions glyphs according to alignment settings Performance: The processor caches intermediate results. Use invalidation methods only when necessary to avoid redundant processing.

types.name: UniTextArrayPool<T>
types.summary: High-performance array pool with thread-local caching and shared overflow storage.
types.remarks: This pool uses a two-tier caching strategy: Thread-local cache: One array per bucket per thread for instant access Shared buckets: Concurrent queues for cross-thread array sharing Arrays are organized into buckets by size (powers of 2 starting at 32). Supported sizes: 32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192, 16384, 32768, 65536. Arrays larger than 65536 are allocated directly without pooling. Usage pattern: var array = UniTextArrayPool<int>.Rent(100); // Gets array of size 128 try { // Use array... } finally { UniTextArrayPool<int>.Return(array); }

typeParameters.name: T
typeParameters.description: The element type of arrays managed by this pool.

methods.name: Rent
methods.summary: Rents an array from the pool with at least the specified length.
methods.remarks: The returned array may contain data from previous use. Clear it if needed. Always call [[Return]] when done to avoid memory leaks.
methods.returns: An array with length greater than or equal to minimumLength. The actual length will be the next power of 2 bucket size.

methods.name: Return
methods.summary: Returns an array to the pool for reuse.
methods.remarks: Only arrays with sizes matching bucket sizes (32, 64, 128, etc.) are accepted. Arrays larger than max bucket size or with non-matching sizes are silently discarded. The array is not cleared before storage. Sensitive data should be cleared manually.

params.name: array
params.description: The array to return. Can be (no-op).

methods.name: GrowDouble
methods.summary: Doubles the capacity of a pooled array when count has reached the current capacity. Copies existing elements, returns the old array to the pool, and updates the reference.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Clears all pooled arrays from both thread-local and shared storage.
methods.remarks: Call this to release memory when the pool is no longer needed, such as during scene transitions or application shutdown.

methods.name: ResetStats
methods.summary: Resets all statistics counters for this pool type.

methods.name: LogStats
methods.summary: Logs pool statistics to the Unity console and resets per-period counters.
methods.remarks: Shows rent/return counts, hit rates, and any rejected returns. Called automatically by [[LogAll]].

methods.name: GetStats
methods.summary: Gets a detailed string report of pool state including per-bucket counts.
methods.returns: A formatted string showing thread-local and shared counts per bucket size.

types.name: UniTextBase

methods.name: SetText

methods.name: SetText

params.name: source

methods.name: SetText

params.name: source

params.name: source

methods.name: CollectRangeEntries
methods.summary: Collects per-line geometric runs of positioned glyphs whose clusters fall inside [startCluster, endCluster). Output bounds are in mesh-local coordinates with X clamped to each line's visible content extent (trailing whitespace excluded via [[width]]). One [[LineRangeEntry]] is emitted per contiguous run within a line — multiple entries per line are possible if the matched clusters are non-contiguous in visual order.

params.description: Pooled list to receive entries (cleared before use).

methods.name: GetRangeBounds
methods.summary: Gets bounding rectangles for a cluster range. One [[Rect]] per contiguous run of glyphs within a line that falls inside [startCluster, endCluster). Trailing whitespace at line ends is excluded (CSS Text §4.1.3). Empty wrapped lines whose break codepoint lies inside the range receive a synthetic narrow rect for caret/selection rendering.

methods.name: EnsureLayoutComputed
methods.summary: Main layout pass. Computes the "preferred" state — [[cachedPreferredHeight]] and an initial [[cachedEffectiveFontSize]] — for the current rect width. Cached by width only: result is independent of rect.height.
methods.remarks: Main-thread only. Canvas variant invokes this from [[CalculateLayoutInputVertical]]; world-space variant has it called implicitly by [[EnsureLayoutFit]].

methods.name: EnsureLayoutFit
methods.summary: Full layout: main pass then, if needed, shrinks [[cachedEffectiveFontSize]] under the current rect.height. Main-pass state comes from the width cache; second pass is cached by rect.height so repeat calls within a frame are free.
methods.remarks: Main-thread only. Canvas variant invokes this from [[SetLayoutVertical]]; world-space variant from the render pipeline before mesh generation.

methods.name: OnDidApplyAnimationProperties
methods.summary: Unity callback invoked after Animator writes animated properties into this component's serialized fields. Subclasses delegate to their composed [[AnimationHandlerBase{T}]] to diff the animated state and aggregate the resulting [[UniTextDirtyFlags]] in a single [[SetDirty]] call.

methods.name: HandleAnimation
methods.summary: Diffs animated fields against the cached baseline through the subclass's animation handler. Implementations should forward to their composed [[AnimationHandlerBase{T}]] instance.

methods.name: EnsureFirstPassComplete
methods.summary: Ensures the first pass (parsing, BiDi, shaping) has run. No-op in the normal pipeline (Phase 1 already ran). Enables LayoutRebuilder.ForceRebuildLayoutImmediate to work outside the pipeline.

types.name: UniTextBuffers
types.summary: Container for all intermediate and final buffers used during text processing.
types.remarks: [[UniTextBuffers]] holds all data produced during the text processing pipeline: codepoints, BiDi levels, text runs, shaped glyphs, line breaks, and positioned glyphs. Performance: All buffers use [[PooledBuffer{T}]] for zero-allocation operation in steady state. Call [[EnsureRentBuffers]] before processing and [[EnsureReturnBuffers]] when done.

methods.name: GetOrCreateAttributeData
methods.summary: Gets or creates typed attribute data for the specified key, incrementing its reference count. The matching [[ReleaseAttributeData]] call decrements; the underlying data is freed only when the count reaches zero. This lets multiple modifier instances safely share one keyed channel — destroying one no longer pulls the buffer out from under the rest.
methods.returns: The existing or newly created attribute data instance.

params.name: key
params.description: The unique key identifying this attribute data.

methods.returns: The attribute data if found; otherwise,.

params.name: key

methods.name: ReleaseAttributeData
methods.summary: Decrements the reference count for key's attribute data and releases the underlying buffer only when the count drops to zero. Pairs one-to-one with [[GetOrCreateAttributeData{T}]].

params.name: key
params.description: The unique key identifying the attribute data to release.

params.name: textLength

types.name: UniTextMeshGenerator
types.summary: Converts positioned glyphs into Unity mesh data for text rendering.
types.remarks: This is the final stage of the text processing pipeline. It takes [[PositionedGlyph]] data from [[TextProcessor]] and generates vertex, UV, color, and triangle data suitable for Unity's mesh system. Key features: Groups glyphs by rendering target to minimize draw calls: one segment per font (Texture2DArray atlas) Uses pooled buffers from [[UniTextArrayPool{T}]] for zero allocations Provides callbacks for text modifiers to inject custom processing Typical usage: generator.SetRectOffset(rect); generator.GenerateMeshDataOnly(positionedGlyphs); var renderData = generator.CollectRenderData(); // Use renderData to render each segment generator.ReturnInstanceBuffers();

methods.name: TrackGlyphKey
methods.summary: Tracks a glyph key for atlas ref counting. Deduplicates automatically. Use for modifier glyphs that don't need cached entry data.

methods.name: UniTextMeshGenerator
methods.summary: Initializes a new instance of the [[UniTextMeshGenerator]] class.

params.name: fontProvider
params.description: The font provider for accessing font assets and materials.

params.name: uniTextBuffers
params.description: The shared buffer container from text processing.

exceptions.description: Thrown when fontProvider or uniTextBuffers is.

methods.name: ScaleGlyphQuad
methods.summary: Scales a glyph quad (4 vertices) around the cursor position and baseline. Used by SizeModifier, SmallCapsModifier, ScriptPositionModifier.

params.name: pivotX
params.description: Cursor position (pen X) — bearing and width scale proportionally from this pivot.

methods.name: EnsureUvBuffer
methods.summary: Allocates and zero-clears a UV effect buffer (channel 2 or 3) if not already allocated.

methods.name: ReturnInstanceBuffers
methods.summary: Returns all instance buffers to the pool and clears the generated data flag.
methods.remarks: Must be called after mesh generation is complete and data has been applied to Unity meshes. Failing to call this method will result in buffer leaks.

methods.name: Dispose
methods.summary: Releases all pooled resources. Call when the generator is no longer needed.

methods.name: EnsureCapacity
methods.summary: Ensures the vertex and triangle buffers have capacity for additional data.
methods.remarks: Called by text modifiers when they need to add geometry beyond the base glyph quads. Automatically grows buffers using the pooled array system if needed.

params.name: additionalTriangles
params.description: Number of additional triangle indices needed.

methods.name: QueueEffectTriangle
methods.summary: Queues the 6 triangle indices for an effect duplicate quad starting at destBaseIdx into the shared pre- or post-face buffer.
methods.remarks: Called by [[ReserveQuad]] when reserving the duplicate's vertex slot. The buffers are flushed once at the end of [[GenerateMeshDataOnly]], producing the final painter order [pre-face 1..N, face, post-face 1..N, line] regardless of how many [[EffectModifier]] instances are active.

methods.name: RequestBandUpgradeIfNeeded
methods.summary: Requests an atlas band upgrade for the current glyph if any effect modifier asked for SDF padding wider than the current tile's computed band. Re-rasterizes the glyph at a larger tile so subsequent frames have room for the requested outline / shadow extent.
methods.remarks: Must be called immediately after [[onGlyph]] for any quad whose outline / shadow / extrude effects should be allowed to grow beyond the default SDF padding. Reads [[currentMaxGlyphExtent]] (effect modifiers write into it during onGlyph) and the face dilate stored in [[Uvs1]][[[faceBaseIdx]]].y.

methods.name: ExpandQuad
methods.summary: Expands a 4-vertex glyph quad outward on all sides by delta (UV-space). Updates both positions and UV0 consistently so the atlas sample stays aligned.
methods.remarks: The position delta is computed as delta * glyphH * fontMetricFactor, using the glyph height stored in Uvs0[baseIdx].w. Caller is responsible for deciding whether expansion is needed.

params.name: baseIdx
params.description: Index of the first vertex of the quad.

params.name: delta
params.description: UV-space padding to add on each side (normalized by glyph height).

methods.name: SetRectOffset
methods.summary: Sets the layout rectangle for text positioning.

params.name: rect
params.description: The rect defining the text layout bounds.

methods.name: GenerateMeshDataOnly
methods.summary: Generates mesh data (vertices, UVs, colors, triangles) from positioned glyphs. Groups by rendering target: SDF fonts in one segment (Texture2DArray), emoji separately.

methods.name: CollectRenderData
methods.summary: Collects raw render data (vertex/UV/triangle array slices + material/order metadata) for every segment produced by the latest mesh generation. Does not build Unity [[Mesh]] objects — consumers (canvas UpdateSubMeshes, world batcher) decide what to do with the raw data.
methods.remarks: SDF and emoji live in the same pooled buffers ([[Vertices]], [[Uvs0]], [[Colors]], [[Triangles]]) as contiguous ranges: SDF in [0, sdfVertexCount), emoji in [sdfVertexCount, sdfVertexCount+emojiVertexCount). Entries carry vertexOffset and vertexCount so consumers can read the right slice. Array references remain valid only until the next [[GenerateMeshDataOnly]] / [[CollectRenderData]] cycle on the same generator (pooled buffers may be regrown or returned). Consumers must not retain references across frames.
methods.returns: Shared list of [[UniTextRenderData]] entries — base SDF and/or emoji segments plus any sub-meshes appended by [[onCollectSubMeshes]] subscribers. The list is reused on the next call; consumers must use/copy immediately.

methods.name: AssignAutoMaterials
methods.summary: Ensures atlas subscription for auto-material management. Must be called on the main thread (creates materials lazily).

properties.summary: Project-wide [[StylePreset]] applied to every [[UniTextBase]] component without per-component opt-in. Behaves as one extra entry appended after each component's local StylePresets list, so local Styles and per-component StylePresets register first and win parse-rule conflicts.
properties.remarks: Assigning fires [[Changed]] with nameof(GlobalStylePreset); subscribed components rebuild their runtime preset copies on the next frame via the standard InvalidateStyles path. Editing the preset's styles list at runtime (via the preset's own [[AddStyle]] / [[RemoveStyle]] / [[ClearStyles]]) is delivered through the asset's own [[Changed]] event, picked up by every component that has it subscribed (local StylePresets entry or this global slot).

Increase for very dense scenes to reduce draw calls; decrease for more fine-grained partial updates when the same group is massive and animated.

The argument is the property name (nameof(...)) of the field that changed, allowing subscribers to filter reactions surgically without per-component snapshot bookkeeping. The sentinel [[All]] means "the entire asset was replaced, re-read everything" and is fired by [[SetInstance]]. types.name: UniTextWorldBatcher
types.summary: Invisible singleton that batches [[UniTextWorld]] components into combined meshes while honoring Unity's sorting model (SortingLayer, OrderInLayer, SortingGroup) so batched text interleaves correctly with SpriteRenderer and other renderers.
types.remarks: Two-level hierarchy: [[BatchGroup]] is a logical grouping by [[BatchKey]] = (materialInstanceId, sortingLayerID, sortingOrder, sortingGroupID). Conceptually "one draw call worth of text". [[BatchShard]] is a physical mesh. A group holds one shard normally; when a group grows past [[WorldBatcherShardTargetVertexCount]] vertices, new shards are added so that structural rebuilds of one shard do not touch unrelated components. Dirty classification: Structural — vertex count changed, entry added/removed, sorting/material changed. Triggers a full rebuild of the affected shard (not the whole group). Positional — transform moved. Writes Position+Normal only, for exactly this entry's slice of the shard's vertex buffer. Attributive — text rebuild without vertex count change (colors/UVs only). Writes the affected attribute streams for this entry's slice. Vertex buffer layout — fixed four streams: Stream 0: Position (float3) + Normal (float3) = 24 bytes/vertex Stream 1: Color (UNorm8×4) = 4 bytes/vertex Stream 2: UV0 (float4) = 16 bytes/vertex Stream 3: UV1 + UV2 + UV3 (float4×3) = 48 bytes/vertex Separate streams let partial updates write only the affected attribute without rewriting unrelated data.

types.name: UniTextWorldRaycaster
types.summary: World-space pointer raycaster for [[UniTextWorld]] components.
types.remarks: Attach to a [[Camera]] to route pointer events (clicks, hover) to all active [[UniTextWorld]] components visible from that camera. Analogous to [[GraphicRaycaster]] for Canvas, but uses direct ray/plane/rect math instead of colliders — no physics dependency at the text level. Hit detection: rect containment in each component's local [[RectTransform]] rect. The full rect is the clickable area (like Canvas raycastTarget); finer-grained glyph-accurate hit testing happens inside UniTextBase.OnPointerClick via [[HitTestScreen]]. Occlusion: results carry distance, so Unity's [[EventSystem]] sorts them against any other raycaster ([[GraphicRaycaster]], PhysicsRaycaster, Physics2DRaycaster) automatically. For scenes without a PhysicsRaycaster but with physical geometry that should block clicks, set [[BlockingObjects]] to TwoD/ThreeD/All — the raycaster will test for blocking colliders between the camera and the hit point before accepting the hit.

types.name: BaseLineModifier
types.summary: Base class for modifiers that render horizontal lines across text (underline, strikethrough).
types.remarks: Subclasses define the vertical offset of the line relative to the baseline. Lines break across wrapped text lines automatically. Decoration quads run through the standard [[onGlyph]] pipeline with [[isVirtualGlyph]] set, so per-glyph modifiers (color, gradient, outline, shadow) apply uniformly to face glyphs and decoration lines.

types.name: BaseModifier
types.summary: Base class for text modifiers — pieces of logic that alter appearance, layout, or behavior of a text range matched by an [[IParseRule]].
types.remarks: Subclass and override the protected hooks ([[OnEnable]], [[OnDisable]], [[OnDestroy]], [[OnApply]], optionally [[PrepareForParallel]]). Lifecycle dispatching is driven by the framework ([[Style]], the parse pipeline, [[CompositeModifier]]) — user code instantiates modifiers and hands them to [[Style]]; it should not invoke the lifecycle itself. Cycle (per parse pass on a UniText component): [[OnEnable]] runs once when the modifier first participates in a cycle — allocate pooled buffers and subscribe to UniText events here. [[OnApply]] runs for every tag/range matched in the current text. [[OnDisable]] runs at the start of the next cycle to unsubscribe event handlers; allocated buffers should stay alive so the next [[OnEnable]] can reuse them. [[OnDestroy]] runs when the modifier is removed from the component (style changed, font reload, component destroyed) — release pooled buffers and any other resources [[OnEnable]] acquired. Guaranteed to run exactly once per [[OnEnable]]-initiated resource acquisition, even when an intervening [[OnDisable]] has already cleared the subscription state.

methods.name: OnEnable
methods.summary: Allocate buffers, subscribe to UniText events, and bring the modifier into the active state. Pairs one-to-one with [[OnDisable]] and [[OnDestroy]].

methods.name: OnDisable
methods.summary: Unsubscribe from UniText events. Buffers and persistent state should remain allocated — [[OnDestroy]] is responsible for releasing them. Runs once per active cycle (at the start of the next parse pass).

methods.name: OnDestroy
methods.summary: Release resources allocated by [[OnEnable]] (pooled buffers, attribute data, registry subscriptions). Always runs after [[OnEnable]] ran at least once, even when the most recent cycle already drained subscriptions via [[OnDisable]].

methods.name: OnApply
methods.summary: Implement the modifier's effect on a codepoint range. Called by the framework for every tag/range matched in the current text after [[OnEnable]].

params.name: parameter
params.description: Parameter forwarded from the tag (e.g. color value); may be when the tag carries no parameter or a composite delivered an absent segment.

properties.name: IsInitialized
properties.summary: between [[OnEnable]] and the next [[OnDisable]]/[[OnDestroy]]: event handlers are currently subscribed. Useful for diagnostics and for nested composites that mirror the child lifecycle.

types.name: BoldModifier
types.summary: Applies bold styling to text using CSS font-weight scale (100-900).
types.remarks: First parameter: optional CSS font-weight (100-900). Without parameter, computes max(700, baseWeight + 300). Second parameter: optional f flag (e.g. <b=700,f>) that forces synthetic bold via SDF dilate (UV1.y) + advance correction, ignoring real bold faces in the Font Family and the wght axis on variable fonts. Without the flag, the pipeline picks the matching real font (variable axis or static face) when available and clears the bold buffer; otherwise the modifier falls back to synthetic bold.

types.name: ColorModifier
types.summary: Applies color to text ranges using hex codes or named colors.
types.remarks: Parameter: a color value in hex or by name. Supported formats: - Hex: #RGB, #RRGGBB, #RRGGBBAA - Named colors: white, black, red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, orange, purple, gray, lime, brown, pink, navy, teal, olive, maroon, silver, gold The alpha channel of the color parameter is multiplied with the component's base alpha (per W3C alpha compositing). A fully opaque parameter inherits the component alpha; a semi-transparent parameter scales it further.

types.name: CompositeModifier
types.summary: Combines multiple modifiers into a single modifier.
types.remarks: Splits the tag parameter by; and passes each segment to the corresponding child modifier. For example, <wobble-color=3,10,1;#FF0000> passes "3,10,1" to the first modifier and "#FF0000" to the second. Child modifiers with no corresponding segment (fewer; groups than modifiers) receive a null parameter and fall back to their defaults.
