types.name: IWordSegmenter
types.summary: Interface for script-specific word segmenters that inject break opportunities into SA-class (Complex Context Dependent) text runs.
types.remarks: Implementations segment a contiguous run of codepoints belonging to a single script and write [[Optional]] at word boundaries. Register via [[Register]]. Registering a segmenter for a script that already has one replaces it.

methods.name: Segment
methods.summary: Segments a span of codepoints and injects Optional break opportunities at word boundaries.

params.name: codepoints
params.description: The full codepoint array of the text.

params.name: start
params.description: Start index of the SA run within codepoints.

params.name: breaks
params.description: Break opportunities array to modify (length = codepoints.Length + 1). breaks[i+1] represents the break opportunity between codepoints[i] and codepoints[i+1]. Must never downgrade an existing Optional or Mandatory break to None.

properties.name: Script
properties.summary: The Unicode script this segmenter handles.

types.name: LineBreakType
types.summary: Specifies the type of line break opportunity according to UAX #14.

fields.name: None
fields.summary: No break allowed at this position.

fields.name: Optional
fields.summary: Break is allowed but not required (soft break).

fields.name: Mandatory
fields.summary: Break is required at this position (hard break after CR, LF, etc.).

types.name: LineRangeEntry
types.summary: A contiguous run of positioned glyphs within a single line whose clusters fall inside a queried range. Bounds are in local mesh coordinates (relative to the text origin), with X clamped to the line's visible content extent (trailing whitespace excluded per CSS Text §4.1.3 via [[width]]).

fields.name: lineIdx
fields.summary: Index of the line in buffers.lines.

fields.name: firstGlyphIdx
fields.summary: Index of the first positioned glyph of this run (inclusive).

fields.name: lastGlyphIdx
fields.summary: Index of the last positioned glyph of this run (inclusive).

fields.name: minX
fields.summary: Left edge of the run in local coordinates, clamped to line content extent.

fields.name: maxX
fields.summary: Right edge of the run in local coordinates, clamped to line content extent.

fields.name: minY
fields.summary: Top edge of the run in local coordinates (uses ascender of glyphs on the line).

fields.name: maxY
fields.summary: Bottom edge of the run in local coordinates (uses descender of glyphs on the line).

types.name: TextDirection
types.summary: Specifies the base text direction for bidirectional text processing.

fields.name: LeftToRight
fields.summary: Left-to-right direction (e.g., Latin, Cyrillic).

fields.name: RightToLeft
fields.summary: Right-to-left direction (e.g., Arabic, Hebrew).

fields.name: Auto
fields.summary: Automatically detect direction from text content using UAX #9.

types.name: UnicodeData
types.summary: Provides access to Unicode character properties and the global data provider.
types.remarks: Contains common Unicode codepoint constants (whitespace, control characters, BiDi marks) and helper methods for character classification. The static [[Provider]] property gives access to the full Unicode property database for script, line break, and grapheme cluster information.

methods.name: IsMandatoryBreakChar
methods.summary: Returns true if the codepoint is a line or paragraph separator that produces a mandatory break (UAX #14 classes BK, CR, LF, NL) and should not be shaped.

methods.name: IsJustifiableWordSeparator
methods.summary: Returns true if the codepoint is a word-separator character eligible for stretching under CSS-style inter-word justification (CSS Text Module Level 3 §6.4.1).
methods.remarks: Modelled on Blink/WebKit/Gecko behaviour: includes ASCII space (U+0020), TAB (U+0009, treated as space for justification), the CJK ideographic space (U+3000), and other Unicode general-category Zs space separators. Explicitly excludes the non-breaking variants — NBSP (U+00A0), NARROW NBSP (U+202F), FIGURE SPACE (U+2007) — which carry "do not break / do not stretch" semantics.

methods.name: GetSimpleUppercase
methods.summary: Returns the simple uppercase mapping for a codepoint, falling back to the codepoint itself when no mapping is defined. Backed by UnicodeData.txt so behavior is identical across Mono/IL2CPP/standard.NET — unlike char.ToUpperInvariant, which has gaps for codepoints such as Greek final sigma U+03C2.
methods.remarks: "Simple" means a single-codepoint default mapping that ignores locale and the conditional rules in SpecialCasing.txt (Turkish dotless I, Lithuanian dot-above, German ß → SS, etc.). Use this in custom BaseModifier implementations for predictable case conversion.

methods.name: GetSimpleLowercase
methods.summary: Returns the simple lowercase mapping for a codepoint, falling back to the codepoint itself when no mapping is defined. See [[GetSimpleUppercase]] for the rationale.

methods.name: GetSimpleTitlecase
methods.summary: Returns the simple titlecase mapping for a codepoint, falling back to the codepoint itself when no mapping is defined. Differs from uppercase only for digraph letters such as U+01C5 (ǅ) — uppercase Ǆ, titlecase ǅ, lowercase ǆ.

methods.name: GetGeneralCategory
methods.summary: Returns the Unicode General Category of a codepoint. Useful for filtering codepoints in custom modifiers — apply only to letters (Lu/Ll/Lt/Lm/Lo), skip combining marks (Mn/Mc/Me), select punctuation (Pc/Pd/Ps/Pe/Pi/Pf/Po), and so on.

methods.name: GetScript
methods.summary: Returns the Unicode Script of a codepoint (UAX #24). Useful for script-conditional modifiers — for example applying a stylistic effect only to Devanagari or only to Han. Values [[Common]] and [[Inherited]] are shared across scripts (punctuation, combining marks).

methods.name: IsExtendedPictographic
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint has the Extended_Pictographic property (UTS #51). Distinct from emoji presentation: pictographic glyphs that may render either as text or as emoji depending on context.

methods.name: IsEmojiPresentation
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint defaults to emoji-style presentation (UTS #51 Emoji_Presentation). Use this to skip emoji glyphs in text-only effects (color, gradient, outline) without relying on the live mesh-pass font.IsColor flag.

methods.name: IsEmojiModifierBase
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint is an emoji that accepts a skin-tone modifier (U+1F3FB..U+1F3FF) immediately after it (UTS #51 Emoji_Modifier_Base).

methods.name: IsDefaultIgnorable
methods.summary: Returns when the codepoint has the Default_Ignorable_Code_Point property (formatting characters, variation selectors, ZWJ/ZWNJ, etc.). Custom modifiers that walk codepoints to compute statistics or apply effects should typically skip these.

types.name: UnicodeScript
types.summary: Unicode Script property values (UAX #24).
types.remarks: Each codepoint belongs to exactly one script. Used by [[ScriptAnalyzer]] to segment text into runs of uniform script for shaping. Some scripts like [[Common]] (punctuation) and [[Inherited]] (combining marks) can appear in text of any script.

fields.name: Unknown
fields.summary: Script could not be determined.

fields.name: Common
fields.summary: Characters used in multiple scripts (punctuation, symbols).

fields.name: Inherited
fields.summary: Combining marks that inherit script from base character.

fields.name: Latin
fields.summary: Latin script (English, Spanish, French, etc.)

types.name: WordSegmentationDictionary
types.summary: Self-contained dictionary asset for word segmentation of a specific script.
types.remarks: Each asset holds a binary double-array trie and the target Unicode script. Add to UniText Settings to enable word segmentation for that script. Create via Tools → UniText → Tools → Dictionary Builder tab.

properties.name: Script
properties.summary: The Unicode script this dictionary targets.

properties.name: IsValid
properties.summary: Returns true if this dictionary contains valid trie data.

types.name: AssetNamedCatalog<TEntry, TAsset>
types.summary: Serializable base for [[INamedCatalog{TEntry}]] implementations that delegate resolution to an explicit ScriptableObject asset reference — useful when multiple components should share the same catalog managed as a project asset.
types.remarks: Subscription to the underlying asset's [[Changed]] event is lazy: this provider attaches only while it has at least one subscriber and detaches when the last unsubscribes, so an unused provider doesn't keep itself alive through the asset's delegate list. The provider also re-binds on inspector edits that change the asset reference ([[OnAfterDeserialize]]).

typeParameters.name: TEntry
typeParameters.description: The entry type stored in the catalog.

typeParameters.name: TAsset
typeParameters.description: The asset type that implements [[INamedCatalog{TEntry}]] for this domain.

properties.name: Asset
properties.summary: The asset used for name resolution. Setting to makes [[TryGet]] return for every name.

types.name: INamedCatalog<TEntry>
types.summary: Resolves named entries by case-insensitive name. Used by every "named catalog" feature in UniText (gradients, inline sprites, inline-object prefabs) so the same set of providers — inline list, shared asset, custom code — composes across all of them.
types.remarks: Concrete implementations decide where the catalog lives — an explicit asset reference, an inline list edited per-modifier, or a custom runtime resolver — and raise [[Changed]] whenever their resolution result changes. The modifier that consults the provider subscribes during its active lifecycle and rebuilds when the event fires. Per-domain marker interfaces ([[IGradientProvider]], [[ISpriteProvider]], [[IObjProvider]]) extend this with no additional members — they exist purely to scope [SerializeReference, TypeSelector] dropdowns and to give domain-specific reading.

typeParameters.name: TEntry
typeParameters.description: The entry type stored in the catalog (e.g. InlineSprite, InlineObject, UniTextGradients.NamedGradient).

methods.name: TryGet
methods.summary: Tries to resolve a name to a catalog entry. Name matching is case-insensitive.
methods.returns: when an entry with the given name was found.

params.name: name
params.description: The lookup name (typically the tag parameter, e.g. jump in <sprite=jump>).

params.name: entry
params.description: The resolved entry when this call returns; otherwise.

methods.name: Enumerate
methods.summary: Enumerates every entry exposed by this provider in catalog order. Used by editor tooling to populate the tag-parameter dropdown. Lazy or runtime-resolved providers may legitimately return an empty sequence.

events.name: Changed
events.summary: Raised whenever the catalog's resolution result may have changed: inline entries added/removed/edited, the underlying asset replaced or its entries mutated, or a custom provider explicitly invalidating its cache. Subscribers should treat this as "invalidate cached resolution and rebuild" — there is no per-source filtering.

types.name: IndexEx
types.summary: Extension methods for parsing [[Index]] from string representation.
types.remarks: Supports C# index syntax: "0" for start-based, "^1" for end-based indices. Used internally for markup parameter parsing.

methods.name: TryParse
methods.summary: Parses a string into a [[Index]].
methods.returns: true if parsing succeeded; otherwise false.

types.name: InlineNamedCatalog<TEntry>
types.summary: Serializable base for [[INamedCatalog{TEntry}]] implementations that keep their entries inline on the owning modifier — edited in the inspector or mutated at runtime via [[SetEntries]], [[Add]], [[Remove]].
types.remarks: Concrete subclasses supply [[GetEntryName]]. The [[Changed]] event fires automatically on every mutation; subscribers stay alive only through their own delegate, no static channels.

typeParameters.name: TEntry
typeParameters.description: The entry type stored in the catalog.

methods.name: SetEntries
methods.summary: Replaces the entry list and raises [[Changed]].

methods.name: Add
methods.summary: Appends one entry and raises [[Changed]].

methods.name: Remove
methods.summary: Removes the first entry with the given name. Returns on success.

methods.name: GetEntryName
methods.summary: Extracts the lookup name from an entry. Return or empty to skip it.

methods.name: RaiseChanged
methods.summary: Raises [[Changed]]. Safe to call without subscribers.

properties.name: Entries
properties.summary: Read-only view over the current entry list.

types.name: NamedCatalogAsset<TEntry>
types.summary: Abstract ScriptableObject base for named-entry catalogs. Subclasses give the catalog a concrete entry type, a CreateAssetMenu path, and (optionally) a payload validity filter for editor enumeration.

typeParameters.name: TEntry
typeParameters.description: The entry type stored in the catalog.

methods.name: Add
methods.summary: Adds an entry and raises [[Changed]]. Marks the asset dirty in the editor.

methods.name: GetEntryName
methods.summary: Extracts the lookup name from an entry. Return or empty to skip it.

methods.name: RaiseChanged
methods.summary: Raises [[Changed]]. Safe to call without subscribers.

properties.name: Entries
properties.summary: Direct read-only view over the entry list. Use [[Add]] to mutate at runtime.

properties.name: Count
properties.summary: Number of entries in the catalog.

properties.name: Names
properties.summary: All entry names exposed by this catalog.

types.name: PooledArrayAttribute<T>
types.summary: A pooled array-based implementation of [[IAttributeData]].
types.remarks: Use this class to store per-codepoint or per-glyph attribute data in modifiers. The underlying array is rented from [[UniTextArrayPool{T}]] for zero-allocation operation.

typeParameters.name: T
typeParameters.description: The type of elements stored in the array.

methods.name: Add
methods.summary: Adds an item to the end of the buffer.

methods.name: EnsureCountAndClear
methods.summary: Ensures the buffer has at least the specified capacity, clearing if newly allocated.

properties.name: Count
properties.summary: Gets the number of elements in the buffer.

fields.name: buffer
fields.summary: The underlying pooled buffer.

types.name: PooledBuffer<T>
types.summary: A value-type wrapper for managing a pooled array with count tracking.
types.remarks: Provides a List-like interface over a pooled array without heap allocations for the container itself. Use [[Rent]] to acquire an array and [[Return]] to release it back to the pool. The [[count]] field tracks how many elements are in use, while [[Capacity]] reflects the actual array length. Operations like [[Add]] automatically grow the buffer.

methods.name: Rent
methods.summary: Rents an array from the pool with the specified capacity. Returns any existing array to the pool first.

methods.name: Return
methods.summary: Returns the array to the pool and resets the buffer.

methods.name: FakeClear
methods.summary: Resets count to zero without clearing data or returning to pool.
methods.remarks: Fast reset for reuse when data clearing is not needed.

methods.name: Clear
methods.summary: Clears the used portion of the array and resets count to zero.

methods.name: ClearData
methods.summary: Clears the used portion of the array without resetting count.

methods.name: ClearAll
methods.summary: Clears the entire backing array (not just [0..count)) and resets count to zero.
methods.remarks: Use this when elements are written via direct [[data]] indexing without updating [[count]] — a pattern used by modifiers whose buffer is read by TextProcessor at arbitrary indices. [[Clear]] and [[ClearData]] only scrub [0..count) which is a no-op for such modifiers when count is zero.

methods.name: EnsureCapacity
methods.summary: Ensures the buffer has at least the specified capacity, growing if needed.

methods.name: EnsureCount
methods.summary: Ensures both capacity and count are at least the specified value.

methods.name: Add
methods.summary: Adds an item to the end of the buffer, growing if necessary.

methods.name: RemoveRange
methods.summary: Removes a range of elements from the buffer.

params.name: index
params.description: The starting index of elements to remove.

params.name: removeCount
params.description: The number of elements to remove.

methods.name: RemoveAt
methods.summary: Removes the element at the specified index, shifting subsequent elements.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the element to remove.

methods.name: Insert
methods.summary: Inserts an item at the specified index, shifting subsequent elements.

params.name: index
params.description: The index at which to insert.

methods.name: SwapRemoveAt
methods.summary: Removes the element at the specified index by swapping with the last element.
methods.remarks: O(1) removal but does not preserve order.

params.name: index
params.description: The index of the element to remove.

methods.name: Sort
methods.summary: Sorts the used portion of the buffer using the specified comparison.

methods.name: Sort
methods.summary: Sorts a range of elements using the specified comparer.

params.name: index
params.description: The starting index of the range to sort.

params.name: length
params.description: The number of elements to sort.

properties.name: Capacity
properties.summary: Gets the capacity of the underlying array (0 if not rented).

properties.name: Span
properties.summary: Gets a span over the used portion of the buffer (0 to count).

fields.name: data
fields.summary: The underlying array. May be if not rented.

fields.name: count
fields.summary: The number of elements currently in use.

types.summary: A reference-type wrapper around [[PooledBuffer{T}]] for scenarios requiring heap allocation.
types.remarks: Use this when you need to store a pooled collection in a field or pass it by reference without boxing. The underlying [[buffer]] is a struct, so modifications are in-place. Provides the same API as [[PooledBuffer{T}]] but as a class for scenarios where value-type semantics are not suitable.

methods.name: PooledList
methods.summary: Initializes a new instance without renting an array.

methods.name: PooledList
methods.summary: Initializes a new instance and rents an array with the specified capacity.

properties.name: Count
properties.summary: Gets the number of elements in the list.

properties.name: Capacity
properties.summary: Gets the capacity of the underlying array.

fields.name: buffer
fields.summary: The underlying buffer storage.

types.summary: Extension methods for parsing [[Range]] from string representation.
types.remarks: Supports C# range syntax: "0..5", "..5", "2..", "^3..^1". Used internally for markup parameter parsing.

methods.summary: Returns true if the expression parses to a range covering the entire text, regardless of which syntactic form was used ("..", "..^0", "0..", etc.).

methods.name: IsWholeText
